title: When Attribution Patching Lies: Diagnosis and a Second-Order Correction

data.title: When Attribution Patching Lies: Diagnosis and a Second-Order Correction
data.research_question: When is attribution patching reliable, how large can its error be, and how should it be corrected?

models_and_data.quote: We evaluate five model families at different scales as shown in Table 1.

models_and_data.item: Models include GPT-2, Pythia, Qwen2.5, Gemma-2, Llama-3.1
Component types: attention heads, pre-activation MLP neurons, Qwen MLP outputs
models_and_data.quote: We analyze attention heads in all models, pre-activation MLP neurons in GeLU models, and MLP layer outputs in Qwen.
We evaluate on the three established circuit benchmarks together with a broader factual-completion setting:

models_and_data.item: Prompt counts for IOI and Greater-Than
models_and_data.quote: IOI uses 50 templated prompts and Greater-Than uses 200 prompts.
All models are hooked with TransformerLens [40].

protocol.step: Screen-Flag-Fix workflow: screen all components, flag unreliable estimates, correct only flagged components
protocol.quote: screen all components with attribution patching, flag unreliable ones via the reliability score, and correct only those with an HVP-based second-order fix.

protocol.step: Compute HVP correction using two backward passes
protocol.quote: Computing δ⊤Hδ requires the Hessian-vector product Hδ, which we obtain via two backward passes [34]:

protocol.step: MS-HVP splits the patch into K sub-steps and applies local second-order corrections
protocol.quote: splits the patch into K equal sub-steps and applies a second-order correction at each intermediate point along the path from a to a+δ.

protocol.step: Selective HVP applies correction only above reliability threshold τ
protocol.quote: compute R̃ for all components, apply HVP correction only to those with R̃ ≥ τ , and trust attribution patching for the rest.

protocol.step: Report 95% confidence intervals via prompt bootstrap
protocol.quote: we report 95% confidence intervals computed from 1,000 bootstrap resamples over prompts.

protocol.step: Compute Hessian-vector products without explicitly forming the Hessian
protocol.quote: Each Hessian–vector product Hδ is computed with a single double backward pass, without ever forming the Hessian explicitly

metrics.name: top-5 relative error
metrics.definition: Mean absolute error on the five components with largest activation-patching effect, normalized by ground-truth score range.
metrics.quote: Our primary metric is top-5 relative error: the mean absolute error of a method’s scores on the five components with largest activation-patching effect, normalized by the ground-truth score range.

metrics.name: reliability score R̃
metrics.definition: Leading omitted quadratic term relative to the first-order attribution-patching estimate.
metrics.quote: R̃ measures the leading omitted term relative to the first-order estimate.

metrics.name: AUROC for detecting >50% relative error
metrics.definition: Area under ROC curve for flagging components whose attribution-patching relative error exceeds 50%.
metrics.quote: ROC curve for detecting >50% relative error. AUC = 0.70 [0.67, 0.73].

metrics.name: top-k overlap
metrics.definition: Fraction of ground-truth circuit heads recovered at top-k ranking.
metrics.quote: Top-k overlap is computed against the activation patching ground truth.

metrics.name: Spearman correlation
metrics.definition: Rank correlation between reliability score and true relative error.

metrics.name: Kendall τ rank correlation
metrics.definition: Global rank correlation of component rankings against activation-patching ground truth.
metrics.quote: Kendall τ rank correlations range from 0.35 on Pythia-410M to 0.72 on Gemma-2-2B factual.

key_results.claim: Standard HVP reduces top-5 relative error substantially on attention heads and pre-activation MLP neurons.
key_results.quote: Standard HVP correction (K=1, cost 2) reduces top-5 relative error by 72–90% on attention heads and 56–67% on pre-activation MLP neurons.

key_results.claim: MS-HVP reduces Llama-3.1-8B IOI error by 82% relative to attribution patching.
key_results.quote: On Llama-3.1-8B IOI, multi-step HVP further reduces error from 8.42% to 3.54%, corresponding to an 82% reduction relative to attribution patching.

key_results.claim: Selective HVP captures most full-HVP gain at low cost.
key_results.numbers: 91% of full-HVP gain at 26% cost; τ=0.1
key_results.quote: Applying HVP only to R̃-flagged components (Figure 6b) captures 91% of full-HVP gain at 26% of the cost (τ =0.1), validating Proposition 2.

key_results.claim: MS-HVP improves GPT-2 Greater-Than top-5 head overlap.
key_results.quote: On GPT-2 Greater-Than, MS-HVP (K=5) increases top-5 head overlap with activation-patching ground truth from 70.1% to 83.2% (+13.1 pp), outperforming both IG and GIM.

key_results.claim: Single HVP pass nearly recovers Gemma-2-2B Greater-Than ranking.
key_results.quote: on Gemma-2-2B Greater-Than, a single HVP pass reduces the top-5 relative error from 7.41% to 0.62%, approaching exact recovery of the activation-patching ranking.

key_results.claim: Standard HVP can overshoot in pathological high-curvature Pythia-410M IOI.
key_results.quote: standard HVP catastrophically overshoots, increasing the error from 22.34% to 47.48%

key_results.claim: MS-HVP at cost 10 beats IG at cost 35 on Pythia-410M IOI.
key_results.quote: On Pythia-410M IOI, MS-HVP with K=5 (cost 10) outperforms IG with S=35 (cost 35), achieving 18.03% versus 18.47% top-5 error (∆ = −0.44 pp, p = 0.022).

limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: The current framework focuses on single-token perturbations.
While we demonstrate consistent gains up to 9B parameters, verifying behaviour at yet larger scales remains an open opportunity.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: HVP does not address circuit completeness or minimality.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: HVP improves component-level attribution accuracy but does not by itself address circuit completeness or minimality

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: SAE encoder nonlinearity adds curvature not analyzed.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: the SAE encoder’s nonlinearity (ReLU or top-k) introduces an additional curvature source whose magnitude we leave to future work.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Joint patches add off-diagonal Hessian contributions not measured.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Joint patches add off-diagonal Hessian contributions

threats_not_stated_by_authors: Paper evaluates Gemma-2-2B/9B, not Gemma 4 E2B; KV-shared layers 15-34 and per-layer embeddings are untested and may change HVP behavior.
CPU-only lab setting may make double-backward HVP/MS-HVP much more expensive than the GPU wall-clock overhead reported in the paper.
Reliability-score thresholds and AUROC may not transfer to Gemma 4 E2B; overall AUROC is only 0.70 and precision at R̃>0.3 is 36%, so false positives could waste CPU compute.
The paper tests attention heads and MLP neurons on IOI/Greater-Than/factual completion, not induction-head or factual-recall tracing with logit lens on Gemma 4 E2B.
Independent per-component patching ignores off-diagonal Hessian interactions, so circuit-level conclusions from selective HVP may still be misleading.
No own code or data URL is provided, limiting exact reproducibility on the lab’s Gemma 4 E2B setup.
data.relevance_to_lab: Directly relevant to the lab’s activation-patching work: it diagnoses when attribution patching is unreliable and proposes HVP/MS-HVP plus a reliability score. It uses Gemma-2-2B/9B and activation patching, so it can inform CPU feasibility and selective correction, but the lab must validate it on Gemma 4 E2B KV-shared layers 15-34, per-layer embeddings, logit lens, induction heads, and factual-recall tracing.

data.title: When Attribution Patching Lies: Diagnosis and a Second-Order Correction
data.research_question: For a given component, when is attribution patching reliable, how large can its error be, and how should it be corrected?

models_and_data.item: IOI dataset: 50 templated prompts with name-swap corruption and Mary as the target
models_and_data.quote: 50 IOI prompts of the form “When Mary and John went to the store, John gave a drink to”, with the indirect object (Mary) as the target.

models_and_data.item: Greater-Than dataset: 200 prompts testing comparison of years
models_and_data.quote: For the Greater-Than circuit [41], we use 200 prompts of the form “The war lasted from the year 17{XX} to the year 17” and measure whether the model assigns higher probability to years greater than XX.

models_and_data.item: Factual-completion sweeps using 20 generic prompts, with selected settings scaled to 55 or 35 prompts
models_and_data.quote: Unless otherwise noted, generic sweeps use 20 factual prompts. We additionally scale selected experiments to 55 prompts for the Pythia-410M attention-head setting and 35 prompts for the Qwen2.5-1.5B attention-head and MLP-output settings.

protocol.step: Create matched clean and counterfactual inputs differing by a controlled corruption.
protocol.quote: Causal localization compares two matched inputs that differ in a controlled way (e.g., swapping a name or replacing a token) and asks which internal components account for the resulting change in output.

protocol.step: Compute the activation-patching causal reference and a first-order attribution-patching estimate.
protocol.quote: Activation patching measures the true causal effect of replacing a with the counterfactual a′ = a + δ, namely ∆ := M (a + δ) − M (a). Attribution patching approximates it using a single backward pass.

protocol.step: Compute each Hessian-vector product with a double backward pass without explicitly forming the Hessian.
protocol.quote: Each Hessian–vector product Hδ is computed with a single double backward pass, without ever forming the Hessian explicitly (implementation details in Appendix E.1).

protocol.step: Score component-level reliability using network-level curvature.
protocol.quote: the reliability score R̃ tracks network-level curvature and accurately localizes failure regions.

protocol.step: For large perturbations, split the patch into K local sub-steps and apply a second-order correction at each step.
protocol.quote: Multi-Step HVP (MS-HVP), which splits the patch into K equal sub-steps and applies a second-order correction at each intermediate point along the path from a to a+δ.

protocol.step: Flag unreliable estimates and apply HVP only to the selected components.
protocol.quote: run attribution patching broadly, threshold R̃, and apply HVP only to the flagged subset.

protocol.step: Compare against Integrated Gradients, Integrated Hessians, GIM, and other attribution-patching refinements.
protocol.quote: We evaluate across five model families (124M–9B parameters), comparing against Integrated Gradients (IG) [10], Integrated Hessians (IH) [11], and GIM [8].

protocol.step: Evaluate uncertainty with prompt-level bootstrap confidence intervals.
protocol.quote: Unless otherwise stated, we report 95% confidence intervals computed from 1,000 bootstrap resamples over prompts.

metrics.name: Top-5 relative error
metrics.definition: Mean absolute error on the five components with the largest activation-patching effect, normalized by the ground-truth score range.
metrics.quote: Our primary metric is top-5 relative error: the mean absolute error of a method’s scores on the five components with largest activation-patching effect, normalized by the ground-truth score range.

metrics.name: Top-k overlap and Spearman correlation
metrics.definition: Agreement between attribution-based head rankings and activation-patching ground-truth rankings.
metrics.quote: We compute attribution-patching and HVP-corrected attributions for all 12 × 12 = 144 attention heads, rank them by magnitude, and compare the resulting rankings against the activation-patching ground truth using top-k overlap and Spearman correlation.

metrics.name: Reliability score
metrics.definition: Relative magnitude of the omitted quadratic correction compared with the first-order attribution estimate.
metrics.quote: R̃ measures the leading omitted term relative to the first-order estimate.

metrics.name: ROC AUC for unreliable-estimate detection
metrics.definition: Area under the ROC curve for detecting attribution estimates with more than 50% relative error, with operating-point recall and precision.
metrics.quote: AUC = 0.70 [0.67, 0.73]. At R̃ > 0.3 (marked), recall is 89% and precision 36%, flagging 40% of components.

metrics.name: Top-K circuit recovery overlap
metrics.definition: Fraction of activation-patching ground-truth heads recovered after ranking heads by attribution magnitude and thresholding at the known circuit size.
metrics.quote: ranking all attention heads by attribution magnitude and threshold at the known circuit size to measure overlap with the activation-patching ground truth

metrics.name: Kendall τ rank correlation
metrics.definition: Global agreement between an attribution-based ranking and the activation-patching reference ranking.
metrics.quote: Kendall τ rank correlations range from 0.35 on Pythia-410M to 0.72 on Gemma-2-2B factual.

metrics.name: Backward-pass cost
metrics.definition: Computational cost measured in backward passes per component per prompt.
metrics.quote: Measured in backward passes per component per prompt, standard attribution patching has cost 1, standard HVP has cost 2, and MS-HVP with K iterations has cost 2K.

key_results.claim: Attribution-patching error is driven by downstream network curvature rather than local component curvature.
key_results.quote: the network-level Hessian exceeds local curvature by 2–66× across three model families, with near-zero correlation (r = 0.04); using f ′′ (z) for correction produces >750% error – worse than no correction at all (Figure 2).

key_results.claim: Standard HVP broadly reduces top-5 relative error for attention heads and pre-activation MLP neurons.
key_results.quote: Standard HVP correction (K=1, cost 2) reduces top-5 relative error by 72–90% on attention heads and 56–67% on pre-activation MLP neurons.

key_results.claim: HVP nearly eliminates top-5 error on Gemma-2-2B Greater-Than.
key_results.quote: on Gemma-2-2B Greater-Than, a single HVP pass reduces the top-5 relative error from 7.41% to 0.62%, approaching exact recovery of the activation-patching ranking.

key_results.claim: Multi-step HVP substantially improves attribution at 8B scale.
key_results.quote: On Llama-3.1-8B IOI, multi-step HVP further reduces error from 8.42% to 3.54%, corresponding to an 82% reduction relative to attribution patching.

key_results.claim: Single-step HVP can overshoot catastrophically when the perturbation exceeds the local Taylor convergence radius, while multi-step HVP restores stability.
key_results.quote: In this regime, standard HVP catastrophically overshoots, increasing the error from 22.34% to 47.48%, exactly as predicted by Corollary 1.

key_results.claim: In the pathological high-curvature setting, MS-HVP is more accurate than much more expensive Integrated Gradients.
key_results.quote: On Pythia-410M IOI, MS-HVP with K=5 (cost 10) outperforms IG with S=35 (cost 35), achieving 18.03% versus 18.47% top-5 error (∆ = −0.44 pp, p = 0.022).

key_results.claim: HVP improves circuit-boundary recovery on GPT-2 Greater-Than.
key_results.quote: On GPT-2 Greater-Than, MS-HVP (K=5) increases top-5 head overlap with activation-patching ground truth from 70.1% to 83.2% (+13.1 pp), outperforming both IG and GIM.

key_results.claim: Selective HVP recovers most of the full-correction benefit at a fraction of the cost.
key_results.quote: Applying HVP only to R̃-flagged components (Figure 6b) captures 91% of full-HVP gain at 26% of the cost (τ =0.1), validating Proposition 2.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The main framework focuses on single-token perturbations, with multi-token semantic corruptions left as a future direction.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: The current framework focuses on single-token perturbations. However, extending to multi-token semantic corruptions is a natural next direction where preliminary results are promising (Appendix E.4).

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Validation is limited to models up to 9B parameters.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: While we demonstrate consistent gains up to 9B parameters, verifying behaviour at yet larger scales remains an open opportunity.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Component-level HVP accuracy does not itself establish circuit completeness or minimality.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: HVP improves component-level attribution accuracy but does not by itself address circuit completeness or minimality – integrating with verification tools is an exciting avenue for future work.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: SAE-encoder nonlinearity introduces an additional curvature source not quantified in the paper.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: the SAE encoder’s nonlinearity (ReLU or top-k) introduces an additional curvature source whose magnitude we leave to future work.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Standard HVP fails in the identified high-curvature regime unless replaced or stabilized with multi-step correction.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: In this regime, standard HVP catastrophically overshoots, increasing the error from 22.34% to 47.48%, exactly as predicted by Corollary 1.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The Greater-Than benchmark cannot be evaluated directly on Gemma because of tokenizer incompatibility.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: — Tokenizer-incompatible: the greater_than task requires patching a single token representing a two-digit number (e.g. “42”), but Gemma’s tokenizer splits it into multiple tokens.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The path-local smoothness bound fails for a non-negligible fraction of GPT-2 component-prompt pairs, concentrated in Layer 0.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: The 17.6% of violations are concentrated in Layer 0, where L̂3 is an order of magnitude larger than mid-network layers (median 0.065 vs. 0.001–0.002).

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Independent component corrections omit off-diagonal Hessian effects that matter for aggregate circuit-level metrics.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: these affect aggregate circuit-level metrics but not per-component ranking (measuring them would require O(n2 ) HVPs).

threats_not_stated_by_authors: Architecture transfer is untested: the paper evaluates Gemma-2-2B and Gemma-2-9B, not Gemma 4 E2B or its KV-shared layers.
CPU feasibility is unknown: all timings use NVIDIA L40S GPUs, and double-backward HVP may have different relative CPU cost and memory behavior.
The evaluated benchmarks do not directly test induction-head identification or factual-recall tracing in the lab's target architecture.
Improved independent component rankings may not transfer to joint-patch behavior, whole-circuit faithfulness, or interactions among simultaneously patched layers.
Random-token and short factual sweeps may not represent naturalistic factual recall, while semantic entity-swap validation covers only a limited subset of models.
Numerical sensitivity is not characterized despite float32 gradients, mixed precision elsewhere, and potential cancellation in the quadratic form.
Prompt-level bootstrap intervals do not quantify variability across models, tasks, corruption draws, random seeds, or implementation choices.
Replication risk remains because no paper-specific code or data URL is supplied, AtP* was reimplemented from its description, and the GIM implementation was modified.
data.relevance_to_lab: The method is directly applicable to Gemma 4 E2B activation-patching workflows: treat each per-layer embedding in the KV-shared layers as a differentiable patched activation, use target-token log-probability or a logit-lens difference as the scalar metric, screen with attribution patching, flag unreliable components using the reliability score, and selectively apply HVP. This could improve localization for induction-head and factual-recall tracing while avoiding full second-order correction on reliable components. The main caveat is that Gemma 4 E2B and CPU performance are not evaluated; double-backward HVP may be substantially more expensive on CPU, and multi-step correction may be needed when perturbations exceed the Taylor convergence radius.
